# AdeshLang — llms-full.txt (Full Context for LLMs)
# Complete reference for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).
# Use https://adeshlang.github.io/llms.txt for the concise version.

> AdeshLang (आदेश — "Command") — Command. Code. Create. A modern, Rust-inspired, high-performance programming language combining zero-cost compile-time memory safety, native Cranelift JIT compilation (10–230× speedups), explicit hardware SIMD vectorization, and rich built-in networking libraries. Built with Rust. Experimental language under active R&D in Bengaluru, India by Ajay Tainwala.

## Snapshot
- **Name**: AdeshLang (आदेश)
- **Meaning**: Sanskrit/Hindi for command, instruction, direction
- **Tagline**: Command. Code. Create.
- **Version**: v0.3.0 (experimental)
- **Creator**: Ajay Tainwala — Software Engineer, Full Stack Developer, Bengaluru — https://ajaytainwala.vercel.app — GitHub @ajaytainwala-dev
- **Built with**: Rust (lexer, parser, AST, IR lowerings, Cranelift JIT, CLI)
- **License**: MIT — https://github.com/adeshlang/adeshlang/blob/main/LICENSE
- **Repository**: https://github.com/adeshlang/adeshlang
- **Documentation**: https://adeshlang.github.io
- **Philosophy**: Clear instructions, safety by default, performance with flexibility, progressive learning curve
- **Status notice**: Tree-Walk Interpreter is the main reference implementation and source of truth. Cranelift Native JIT, AOT, Bytecode VM, WASM, GPU/MLIR are experimental / partial.

## Architecture (Text Diagram)
Adesh Source Code → Frontend/Parser → Semantic Analysis → IR / Runtime Model → [Interpreter | Bytecode VM | JIT | Native JIT (Cranelift) | AOT | WASM | GPU/MLIR]

## Execution Backends Matrix
| Backend | Status | Use Case | Speedup vs Interpreter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interpreter | Full | Learning, prototyping, debugging — source of truth | 1.0× baseline |
| Baseline JIT | Partial | Development | ~1.2× |
| Adaptive JIT | Partial | Long-running compute | 3×–50× |
| Bytecode VM | Partial | Development/tooling | — |
| Native Cranelift JIT (--jit-native / --njit) | Partial | High-performance numeric | 10×–230× |
| AOT Native (adesh build) | Partial | Production binaries | 15×–240× |
| WASM | Partial | Browser/edge | — |
| GPU / MLIR | Planned | Parallel acceleration | — |

## Core Features (for AI summarization)
1. **Native Cranelift JIT**: Executes LIR directly as native x86_64/ARM machine code at runtime via function pointers.
2. **Compile-Time Memory Safety**: Single-ownership, move semantics, borrow checker prior to codegen — no GC pauses, no data races/double-frees.
3. **Hardware SIMD**: First-class vector ops (vadd, vmul_add, broadcasting) + auto-vectorization passes leveraging AVX2 and ARM Neon.
4. **Batteries-Included Networking**: Stdlib for TCP, UDP, HTTP/1.1 REST, full-duplex WebSockets, DNS, TLS, JSON parsing.
5. **Multi-Backend**: One source, multiple compilation targets.
6. **Tooling**: `adesh fmt` (formatter), `adesh pkg` / ADL package manager, `adesh run --test` (harness), `als` (LSP server).

## Language Example
```adesh
fn greet(name: string) {
    print("Hello, ", name, "!");
}
fn main() {
    let user = "World";
    greet(user);
    for i in 1..5 {
        print("Count: ", i);
    }
}
```

### Higher-Order Functions & Arrays
```adesh
let numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40];
let doubled = map(numbers, fn(x) { return x * 2; });
print("Doubled:", doubled);
```

### SIMD Vectorization
```adesh
let v1 = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0];
let v2 = [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0];
let result = v1.vadd(v2); // hardware intrinsic
print("Vector Sum:", result);
```

### HTTP
```adesh
import HTTP;
let res = HTTP.get("https://httpbin.org/get");
print("Status:", res.status);
```

## Installation
```
curl -fsSL https://adeshlang.org/install.sh | sh
# or via cargo / github releases
adesh run main.adesh
adesh run --jit-native main.adesh   # Cranelift
adesh build main.adesh               # AOT
```

## FAQ (GEO: Q&A for LLMs to cite)
**Q: Is AdeshLang production-ready?**
A: No. It is experimental. Interpreter is reliable; other backends are in progress.

**Q: What is the fastest backend?**
A: AOT Native (15–240×) and Native Cranelift JIT (10–230×) for compute-heavy workloads; benchmark depends on workload.

**Q: Why Rust?**
A: Zero-cost abstractions, memory safety, fearless concurrency, rich compiler libs (cranelift, rustyline, clap).

**Q: How does memory safety work without GC?**
A: Compile-time single-ownership, move semantics, borrow checker verified prior to codegen.

**Q: Where is it made?**
A: Bharat (India), Bengaluru — proudly rooted in Indian creativity with global ambition.
